assessor_label: Claude Fable 5.1 Thinking High (Anthropic) — fresh context, independent of the provisional scoring
exposure_disclosure: None of the listed contaminating files were opened. One filename-only grep hit (rg -l for 'cahn.hilliard') listed morphoeval/build_turing_open_problems.py among matching paths; its contents were not read and no score was seen. Repo inspection was limited to models/, datasets/ READMEs/reference JSON keys, morphoeval/scout_literature.py, measure_outputs.py, lean/, predictions/ registry header, and wave-vector-analysis test CSVs.

tool_fit.why: models/1981-murray-bos-taurus-turing-wavelength.py has RD + Eden generators, coat masks and a paired harness as-is; Cahn-Hilliard (adaptable from 2002-sumper diatom phase-sep) and buckling (1975-richman) need adapting; the discriminator/classifier itself is new code.

data_in_hand.why: 10 SHA-pinned Holstein specimens in datasets/bos_taurus_turing_wavelength (1 + 9 extra_specimens); synthetic ground truth is generated in-run.

falsifiable_done.why: Locked held-out accuracy + confusion matrix is taste-free; 'definite class for the Holstein set' needs a pre-registered posterior/margin criterion or it becomes arguable.

compute_in_repo.why: Four 2D generators x ~100 seeds, Minkowski/PSD features and a numpy LDA/kNN run in hours on the numpy/scipy stack; no wet lab.

isolation.why: New script + new result files; the predictions/ registry row touches a shared CSV/JSON that parallel agents also append to.

time_to_verdict.why: One long sitting: generator adaptation, feature pipeline, training, blind application.

not_blocked.why: OP-11 found RD-vs-Eden indistinguishable on these masks (p=0.91); not the same multi-feature route, but a recorded negative on the Holstein leg.

evidence_for.text: Synthetic ground truth is generated in-run, so the registered held-out accuracy is measurable with no external dependency.
Three of four generators (RD, Eden, phase separation, buckling) already exist in some form in models/; only adaptation, not invention, is needed.
Candidate features (radial PSD shape, Minkowski functionals, junction statistics) are standard and implementable in numpy/scipy in-repo.

evidence_against.text: OP-11 p=0.91 on the same masks suggests RD vs Eden is near-indistinguishable at photo resolution, so the Holstein leg may land in an indeterminate region.

Synthetic-to-photograph domain shift (mask resolution, body curvature, Otsu/colour segmentation artefacts) can dominate the features; a scorer may dispute whether the Holstein class reflects mechanism.
'Returns a definite class' is a second, taste-prone clause; unless a margin is locked, an ambiguous posterior yields a contested rather than decisive outcome.

problems.note: Crux: the synthetic confusion matrix is cheap and decisive; the blind Holstein application is where the hypothesis will be fought over. Packet says CH/buckling generators 'must be written fresh' but non-template phase-separation (2002-sumper) and buckling (1975-richman) scripts exist to adapt.

tool_fit.why: scout_literature.py --query is only an OpenAlex search; the 1952 dispersion/d_c = 3.9271 is for the Gray-Scott Jacobian and does not transfer to WNT/DKK, Nodal/Lefty etc. kinetics, so the classifying computation is not a run-as-is tool.

data_in_hand.why: Public literature; Nodal/Lefty (Mueller 2012) and GDF5/NOG (Grall 2024) are known; others need targeted FRAP/FCS lookups and may be unmeasured (which the packet counts as a finding).

falsifiable_done.why: Pre-registered class counts are checkable, but assigning 'two-node-feasible' needs a kinetics-specific threshold; 'bounded D' and class boundaries carry taste.

compute_in_repo.why: Dispersion evaluation is trivial; the effort is reading, not compute.

isolation.why: New table under datasets/ plus one registry row in a shared file.

time_to_verdict.why: >=6 systems with DOI-cited D values is one long literature sitting; feasible but easily spills over.

not_blocked.why: No prior repo attempt at a census; scout-063 ZF-TUR-01 is a related negative, not a refutation of this route.

evidence_for.text: Nodal/Lefty D values are measured (Mueller 2012: ~0.7 vs ~18 um^2/s), giving at least one clean two-node-feasible row.
GDF5/NOG (Grall 2024) is a published no-differential-diffusion case, populating the 'needs immobile third node' class.
The 'D unmeasured' class is trivially populated (WNT/DKK in skin, EDAR/WNT/BMP ridges), so the >=6-row and three-class coverage conditions are easy to meet.

evidence_against.text: Two-node feasibility depends on the kinetic Jacobian, not just the D ratio; using the Gray-Scott d_c as a universal gate makes class assignments disputable.
The three classes are not mutually exclusive once network topology is considered (Marcon 2016), so a scorer can contest the pre-registered counts.
Extracellular D estimates differ 10-100x between FRAP, FCS and modelling fits for the same morphogen, so single rows can flip class.

problems.note: Crux: the table will be assembled, but 'two-node-feasible' needs a per-system Jacobian or a stated generic bound; the packet's reliance on the GS d_c is the weak link.

tool_fit.why: 1952-turing-morpho.py supplies Jacobian/dispersion and Lean d_c for Gray-Scott only; the Latin-hypercube sweep over Tica's two- and three-node kinetics is a new script.

data_in_hand.why: Published fractions and bounds (Tica 2024 Fig. 2A / Table S5; Scholes 2019) are one SI fetch away; no biological data.

falsifiable_done.why: Within one order of magnitude and >=10x ordering is a crisp numeric gate.

compute_in_repo.why: Vectorised linear stability over ~1e7 LHS samples is hours in numpy; fractions as small as 3.5e-6 need that sample size.

isolation.why: New sweep script under morphoeval/ or models/ plus a shared-registry row.

time_to_verdict.why: One sitting if the SI equations are adopted directly.

not_blocked.why: scout-034's Pearson (F,k) sweep is a different target; nothing recorded on parameter volume.

evidence_for.text: Pure linear-stability computation with no data dependency; result is deterministic given equations, bounds and sampler.
The one-order-of-magnitude / >=10x gate is numeric and leaves no room for interpretation.
LHS sampling is embarrassingly parallel and fits the repo's numpy stack.

evidence_against.text: The packet's 'repo two-node kinetics' (Gray-Scott) are not Tica's two-node circuit; a mismatch would be ambiguous between non-reproduction and different kinetics unless the published equations are used verbatim.
Turing fractions are highly sensitive to bounds and log-vs-linear sampling; small convention differences shift fractions by orders of magnitude.
Depends on parsing Tica 2024 SI (Table S5) correctly; a transcription error silently changes the verdict.

problems.note: Crux: adopt Tica's exact ODEs and bounds, not the repo's Gray-Scott; otherwise the ratio test is a comparison of different models. The done should specify log-uniform sampling as in the paper.

tool_fit.why: scout_literature.py --taxon is a 5-hit Wikimedia Commons search; ridge/Y-junction counting exists (morphoeval/verify_image_fitness.py, 1995-kondo script), but no tool finds a sized ontogenetic series.

data_in_hand.why: Not in repo (one Commons juvenile photo without length metadata); no named public series other than Kondo-Asai 1995 Fig. 1 is identified.

falsifiable_done.why: All stages within +-1 stripe is crisp; stripe counting on curvilinear juveniles has recorded over-count taste (scout-032).

compute_in_repo.why: Counting and the L/lambda_c prediction are trivial compute; the cost is acquisition, not infrastructure.

isolation.why: New datasets/ folder with SHA-pinned images plus a registry row.

time_to_verdict.why: Finding >=6 stages with body length is an open-ended hunt; not reliably one sitting.

not_blocked.why: scout-031 already searched for a Kondo ontogenetic series and found only one adult photo; scout-032 flagged counter over-count.

evidence_for.text: If a sized series exists, the locked N = round(L/lambda_c) test is immediately decisive.
Aquarium-trade and FishBase juvenile records sometimes attach body length in cm, giving a plausible, if thin, source.

evidence_against.text: Public juvenile angelfish photographs almost never carry body-length metadata; the >=6-stage requirement with size is the binding constraint.
scout-031 already attempted the series search and recorded failure beyond a single photo.
Stripe counting on C-shaped curvilinear juveniles is taste-laden (scout-032 over-count), weakening the +-1 gate.
Conjunctive hypothesis: both acquisition and scoring must succeed.

problems.note: Crux: the series does not exist in any named public place; without it the route stalls before scoring. The packet omits the existing models/1995-kondo-pomacanthus-stripe-insertion.py and its polar-sector solver, which would be the natural prediction engine.

tool_fit.why: scout_literature.py only surfaces papers; no extraction tool; the regression is trivial but the deciding step (measured wavelengths) has no repo tool.

data_in_hand.why: Catalog *_turing_wavelength empirical_series are template artefacts and excluded; >=10 taxa of DOI-cited wavelength + body size must be extracted by hand from heterogeneous sources.

falsifiable_done.why: Slope CI vs 0 / vs 1 / neither is crisp, but mixing follicle spacing, stripe period, digit spacing and rugae into one 'wavelength' is a design choice a scorer can reject.

isolation.why: New extraction table under datasets/ and a new script.

time_to_verdict.why: Ten taxa with both measurements and DOIs is a multi-hour to multi-day extraction.

not_blocked.why: scout-048/062 discredited the template curves but no scaling test has been tried.

evidence_for.text: Once the table exists the locked slope test returns one of three pre-defined classes, so the statistical step is decisive by construction.
Some measurements are readily citable (Kondo-Asai angelfish stripe period, mouse/human hair follicle spacing, mouse digit spacing).

evidence_against.text: Pooling different pattern types across taxa makes the slope uninterpretable; a scorer can reject 'neither' or 'scaling' as an artefact of heterogeneity.
Turing's intrinsic-wavelength claim is about a fixed system; an interspecies regression conflates ontogenetic scaling with evolutionary retuning of kinetics, so the test does not isolate the gap.
>=10 taxa with both DOI-cited wavelength and body size is a heavy extraction with no tooling.

problems.note: Crux: the regression is cheap but the inferential design (cross-taxon, mixed pattern types) does not cleanly test Turing's intrinsic wavelength; restricting to one pattern type (e.g. fish stripe period) would sharpen it at the cost of taxon count.

tool_fit.why: Packet is wrong that no BSW model exists: models/2014-raspopovic-bmp-sox9-wnt-digits.py runs the 3-node network on a growing polar-fan FEM mesh with AER-FGF wavelength modulation, noise ICs and ray counts; models/2012-sheth-hox-turing-polydactyly.py gives the Hox-dose series. A 200-random-IC wrapper and five-ray counter is still new.

data_in_hand.why: Published parameters already encoded in the scripts and datasets/bmp_sox9_wnt_digits reference JSON; no wet data.

falsifiable_done.why: Exactly five rays in >=95% of 200 runs and Hox-dose ordering are numeric gates; a pre-registered ray-counting rule is needed.

compute_in_repo.why: 200 FEM growing-domain runs are hours on the repo stack; feasible but not trivial.

isolation.why: New wrapper script importing or re-implementing existing functions; new output files.

time_to_verdict.why: One long sitting once the wrapper runs.

not_blocked.why: No prior repo attempt at the reproducibility fraction.

evidence_for.text: A growing-domain BSW solver with gradient modulation and digit-ray counting already exists in models/, so the deciding simulation is mostly a loop over seeds.
Pure simulation with a sharp numeric threshold; either >=95% or not is observable regardless of outcome.
The Sheth Hox-dose wavelength law is already implemented, making the polydactyly ordering clause cheap to score.

evidence_against.text: The existing script's F->D wavelength mapping is an admitted modelling choice, not Raspopovic's equations; a failed 95% could be attributed to model unfaithfulness rather than refuting the hypothesis.
Ray counting at the distal arc (what counts as a ray vs a branch) needs a locked rule; otherwise the fraction is contestable.
200 FEM runs may exceed a single loop's wall clock on a laptop.

problems.note: Crux: the packet's tool_route is out of date; BSW + Hox-dose scripts exist. Likely outcome is failure of the 95% gate (RD from noise rarely locks topology), which is still decisive provided the model is accepted as faithful.

tool_fit.why: models/1984-wolfram-conus-textile-rule30.py has run_meinhardt_conus (PDE kymograph), Rule 30/Rule 90 steps, the Ermentrout-Oster gate and compute_2d_chiral_and_anf_observables; only the 3-neighbourhood transducer-table extraction is new.

data_in_hand.why: Everything is in repo (PDE, CA, Lean gate in morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean, 2D observables).

falsifiable_done.why: Agreement fractions above a locked threshold are crisp, but the coarse-graining (PDE steps per CA tick, cell width, threshold) is not fixed by the done and drives the result.

isolation.why: New script importing from a 12.8k-line module; must avoid its top-level side effects but no shared file edits are required.

not_blocked.why: No transducer table extracted before; the script already reports chirality_meinhardt = 0.0000 vs Rule 30 -0.4973, a partial prior negative on the 2D clause but not a refutation of the route.

evidence_for.text: All inputs and observables are in repo and deterministic; the test can run end to end today.
The 2D chirality observable is already computed (Meinhardt 0.0000 vs R30 -0.4973), so half of the hypothesis is effectively already decided negative.
The empirical 8-row transducer table is a few dozen lines of code over an existing kymograph.

evidence_against.text: The 1D agreement fraction is sensitive to sampling interval and threshold; without locking the coarse-graining a scorer can argue any rule could be fit or missed.
The Meinhardt PDE is left-right symmetric so it cannot induce the chiral Rule 30; the test is nearly foregone, inviting a 'trivially negative' objection.

problems.note: Crux: a symmetric PDE should map to a symmetric (Rule 90-like or additive) rule, so expect a decisive negative on Rule 30; lock the coarse-graining scale and threshold in the registry before running.

tool_fit.why: No repo tool can build or assay a eukaryotic synthetic circuit; the modelling satellite is not the deciding evidence.

data_in_hand.why: Deciding data is wet-lab output not obtainable here.

falsifiable_done.why: The wet-lab done is exact, but no scorer in this repo can check it.

compute_in_repo.why: Requires a wet lab; only a regime map of the Sekine model runs here and it does not decide the problem.

isolation.why: A satellite regime-map script would be new files only, but it is not the deliverable.

time_to_verdict.why: No verdict reachable in this repo on any timescale.

evidence_for.text: A Turing-vs-solitary regime map of the Sekine competitive-inhibition model is computable in-repo as a satellite.

evidence_against.text: The definition of done is a wet-lab construct with biological replicates; the repo has no wet capability.
The packet itself states the deciding data is not obtainable here.
The hypothesis asserts the repo decides a question that is settled only by experiment.

problems.note: Crux: scope. Keep as a tracked external problem; the only in-repo contribution is a modelling regime map, which should be registered as a separate, non-deciding satellite.

tool_fit.why: wave-vector-analysis/ provides the spark_tracks schema and embryo_units.py; no spectral or surrogate tool exists, so the deciding script is new.

data_in_hand.why: test_data/spark_tracks_qc_folder31.csv (453 frames, embryos A/B) and _folder33.csv (371 frames, embryo A) are in repo at 1 fps with x,y,t per event.

falsifiable_done.why: Per-embryo surrogate test at a locked false-positive rate is crisp; 'fit the driven-front line' and 'secondary ridge' detection need pre-specified estimators.

compute_in_repo.why: Binned (x,t) event field, 2D FFT and ~1000 phase-randomised surrogates run in minutes.

isolation.why: New spectral script and output files; registry row is the only shared touch.

not_blocked.why: scout-036 proposed but never ran spectra; OP-07/08 found orientation, not wave features, carried signal — a related negative.

evidence_for.text: Data is in repo and the surrogate test is self-contained, so a per-embryo present/absent call at the locked rate is procedurally guaranteed.
Phase-randomised surrogates give a calibrated null regardless of the data's idiosyncrasies.

evidence_against.text: Sparse point events (~3-5k per recording) at 1 fps give a poorly resolved (k, omega) surface with Nyquist 0.5 Hz; an 'absent' call is largely a power statement, which a scorer may deem non-decisive.
Only ~3 embryo recordings are in repo, so the pooled verdict rests on very few units.
Poke-triggered fronts are broadband and single-shot; separating a Turing-Hopf ridge from front harmonics and coordinate-system artefacts (COORDINATE_SYSTEM_WARNING.md) is ambiguous.
Prior blind tests (OP-07/08) found no wave-feature signal, lowering the chance of a positive and raising the chance of an under-powered negative.

problems.note: Crux: the test will return a number, but with ~3 embryos and 1 fps sparse events the 'absent' outcome is weak evidence; pre-register a power analysis on synthetic Turing-Hopf fields so a negative is interpretable.

tool_fit.why: No vegetation RD (Klausmeier) or termite-territory model in repo; 2015-ocko-termite-mound script is about convection, not territories; only the generic 2D RD solver base is reusable.

data_in_hand.why: Published pair-correlation/Voronoi statistics (Getzin 2016) are one fetch away; georeferenced aerial imagery is not a single named public fetch.

falsifiable_done.why: Locked thresholds are crisp, but the gap itself notes pattern statistics have not separated the mechanisms, so the gate may be structurally non-discriminating.

compute_in_repo.why: Both models are simple PDE/agent simulations that run in hours once written.

isolation.why: All new scripts and data folders.

time_to_verdict.why: Two new models plus data acquisition is more than one sitting.

evidence_for.text: Both a scale-dependent-feedback vegetation model and a Voronoi territory model are small to implement.
Getzin et al. publish pair-correlation and Voronoi statistics numerically, reducing imagery dependence.

evidence_against.text: Tarnita 2017 shows both mechanisms (and their combination) yield the same hexagonal statistics; pattern statistics alone cannot decisively favour one, so the hypothesis is likely undecidable at any threshold.
Public georeferenced aerial imagery suitable for point extraction is not one named fetch and may have licensing limits.
Nothing exists in repo; two models plus a data pipeline is a multi-day build before the first verdict.

problems.note: Crux: the packet's own gap statement undermines the done — static spatial statistics do not separate RD from termite engineering; a decisive test would need dynamics (e.g. rainfall-response or gap-recovery series), which are not in scope here.
